open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES representation
open_points.question: How does State 6 represent the complete cookie attributes that `owner_interface` must apply when it sets the owner-session cookie?
options: A structured cookie-attributes model consumed by the HTTP serializer.
A fixed serialized Set-Cookie attribute suffix.
Separate typed constants for each attribute, collected by `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`.
open_points.default_guess: Use a structured immutable cookie-attributes model so the serializer, rather than application code, owns header syntax.
consequences: A structured model permits validation and avoids embedding header syntax in policy data, but requires a model and serializer contract.
A serialized suffix is simple but makes quoting, ordering and validation part of the constant's value.
Separate constants expose more imports and enlarge the dependency surface.
open_points.requirement: On sign-in, the session cookie set: not readable by scripts, only to Registry's origin, and always HTTPS-only (A13 rule 1; owner, 2026-11-17), and never sent with a request another site started (`SameSite=Strict`; owner, 2026-11-24).

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: context-sensitive owner-page encoding
set_aside.text: an element's content, an attribute's value, a value of a link's query
set_aside.question: How will State 6 distinguish and serialize stored values placed in element content, attribute values and URL-query components while preserving each value exactly?
options: Declare distinct typed renderer operations for text, attributes and query parameters.
Declare one renderer operation with an explicit output-context argument.
Use structured page and URL models whose serializers choose the encoding from the destination field.
set_aside.default_guess: Use structured page and URL models with context-specific serializers, preventing callers from selecting an unsafe encoder.
consequences: Distinct operations make misuse visible but enlarge the rendering API.
A context argument keeps one API but permits callers to supply the wrong context.
Structured models provide the strongest construction-time separation but require more model declarations.
set_aside.requirement: The owner interface renders every stored value as text: escaped for the place it appears in, never as markup or script, whoever wrote it.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: content security policy serialization
set_aside.text: every page forbids every script by its content security policy
set_aside.question: What exact HTTP representation will State 6 use for the content security policy that forbids scripts on every owner-interface page?
options: A response header containing `script-src 'none'` together with the other required directives.
A stricter response header such as `default-src 'none'` with explicit allowances for required non-script resources.
A response header plus a redundant HTML meta policy.
set_aside.default_guess: Use a response header with `default-src 'none'` and explicitly allow only the non-script resources the server-rendered pages require.
consequences: A focused `script-src 'none'` satisfies the script prohibition but leaves unrelated resource classes to other directives or browser defaults.
A default-deny policy is stronger but requires every legitimate image, style, form and navigation source to be declared.
A redundant meta policy increases complexity and cannot replace header-only CSP features.
set_aside.requirement: The owner interface sends no script of its own (R0-29) and forbids the browser to run any, by its content security policy.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store statement backend
set_aside.text: Every value of a record reaches the store through the one statement backend the specification fixes, which fills value places only (rule 3)
set_aside.question: Which hidden State 7 procedure will ensure that every supplied or imported value reaches SQLite only as a bound value and never as statement structure?
options: Use parameterized SQLite statements exclusively for values.
Use a restricted query builder that emits fixed statements and bound parameters.
Generate a closed catalogue of prepared statements and prohibit ad-hoc statement construction.
set_aside.default_guess: Generate a closed catalogue of parameterized statements and pass all record values as bindings.
consequences: Parameterized statements are direct and conventional but require every persistence path to follow the rule.
A query builder can centralize the guarantee but adds a dependency and its own correctness surface.
A closed prepared-statement catalogue gives the strongest audit boundary but requires more generated persistence infrastructure.
set_aside.requirement: A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an operator or syntax.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: import serialization and data-only parser
set_aside.text: an import file whose values hold markup, a statement of the store's query language and text written as program code is read into those same values as text, unchanged, and nothing in it is executed or evaluated (rule 4).
set_aside.question: What exact import serialization and non-evaluating parser will State 6 declare?
options: A versioned JSON document parsed by a standard data parser.
A versioned declarative archive format with a fixed schema and no executable extensions.
The legacy export's existing data format, formally declared with a strict parser and closed schema.
set_aside.default_guess: Declare the legacy export's data format as a versioned closed schema and parse it with a non-evaluating data parser.
consequences: JSON has widely available safe parsers but may require conversion from the actual legacy export.
Another declarative format may fit the source better but adds parsing and dependency choices.
Keeping the legacy format minimizes migration tooling changes but requires its grammar and malformed-input behavior to be specified precisely.
set_aside.requirement: The import file is read as data with a size limit of 50 MB, 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes (owner, 2026-11-11); nothing in it is executed or evaluated, and a file over the limit is refused before any of it is parsed.
